extracted.intended_audience: members of the public and stakeholders invited to submit comments on the FTC petition (e.g., horseracing industry participants, regulated parties, advocacy groups, and interested individuals)
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and procedural requirements for submitting public comments on the Federal Trade Commission's published petition for rulemaking (docket FTC-2024-0030). Covers how to file, deadlines, confidentiality limits, and where to view documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments must identify the petition docket number and meet the filing deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments must identify the petition docket number and be filed by August 9, 2024.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments must be timely and responsive; any person may submit comments in support of or in opposition to the petition. All timely and responsive comments submitted in connection with this petition will become part of the public record. The Commission will not consider the petition's merits until after the comment period closes. (Docket number: FTC-2024-0030.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit comments using the Federal eRulemaking Portal (Regulations.gov)
rubrics_metrics.description: You may view the petition (docket FTC-2024-0030) and submit written comments concerning its merits by using the Federal eRulemaking Portal at https://www.regulations.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the online instructions for submitting comments. You may read background documents or comments received at https://www.regulations.gov at any time. Do not submit sensitive or confidential information through the portal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not include sensitive personal information in comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not include sensitive personal information such as Social Security numbers; dates of birth; driver's license or other state identification numbers; passport numbers; financial account numbers; or credit or debit card numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You are solely responsible for ensuring your comment does not include any sensitive personal information. Such information should be omitted because comments are placed on the publicly accessible regulations.gov website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not include sensitive health information in comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not include sensitive health information, such as medical records or other individually identifiable health information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You are solely responsible for making sure your comment does not include sensitive health information, since comments will be publicly accessible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not include trade secrets or privileged commercial/financial information
rubrics_metrics.description: Your comment should not include any 'trade secret or any commercial or financial information which . . . is privileged or confidential' as provided by section 6(f) of the FTC Act (15 U.S.C. 46(f)) and FTC Rule 4.10(a)(2) (16 CFR 4.10(a)(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies may redact or withhold certain submissions (or portions thereof). If you submit information that may be privileged or confidential, it may be subject to withholding or redaction under applicable law and regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments become part of the public record and may be redacted or withheld
rubrics_metrics.description: All timely and responsive comments submitted will become part of the public record; agencies review all submissions and may choose to redact or withhold certain submissions (or portions thereof). Submitted comments may not be available to be read until the agency has approved them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because your comment will be placed on the publicly accessible website at regulations.gov, you are solely responsible for making sure it does not contain sensitive or confidential information. The notice also indicates the number of comments received (e.g., 1,109) and that comments may be processed for public viewing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of the petition is procedural and does not alter legal status
rubrics_metrics.description: Publication of the petition is pursuant to the Commission's Rules of Practice and Procedure and does not affect the legal status of the petition or its final disposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pursuant to section 18(a)(1)(B) of the FTC Act (15 U.S.C. 57a(1)(B)) and FTC Rule 1.31(f) (16 CFR 1.31(f)), the petition has been placed on the public record for a period of 30 days. The Commission will not consider the petition's merits until after the comment period closes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify official Federal Register/PDF for legal research; XML site is informational
rubrics_metrics.description: The FederalRegister.gov site displays a prototype XML rendition and is not an official legal edition; users relying on it for legal research should verify results against an official edition of the Federal Register on govinfo.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each document posted includes a link to the corresponding official PDF file on govinfo.gov. Until the Administrative Committee of the Federal Register grants official status, the XML rendition does not provide legal notice to the public or judicial notice to the courts; verify contents against the official PDF.
